name: Santan (coconut milk), thick
notes: The quiet cost of most Malaysian curries. A cup of gulai can carry 400 kcal of this alone.

name: Santan, diluted (light)
notes: Diluting is the single easiest cut in local cooking.

name: Palm Oil / Minyak Masak
notes: What most local frying uses. Every tablespoon absorbed is ~124 kcal.

name: Olive Oil
notes: Better fat profile, identical calories. Oil is oil for energy.

name: Coconut Oil
notes: Mostly saturated. No metabolic free lunch despite the marketing.

name: Sesame Oil
notes: Used for aroma, so a teaspoon is usually enough.

name: Butter
notes: Roti bakar with butter and kaya is ~250 kcal before the bread.

name: Ghee / Minyak Sapi
notes: Used in briyani and murtabak.

name: Margarine / Planta
notes: Check the label — hydrogenated versions carry trans fat.

name: Lard
notes: Used in some Chinese kopitiam cooking.

name: Mayonnaise
notes: Salad turns into a fat delivery system fast.

name: Mayonnaise, light
notes: Roughly a third of full-fat.

name: Sambal Belacan
notes: Chilli, belacan, minimal oil. Cheap flavour.

name: Sambal Tumis
notes: Fried in oil, so far denser than raw sambal.

name: Kicap Manis (sweet soy)
notes: Mostly sugar. Two spoons in mee goreng adds up.

name: Kicap Masin (light soy)
notes: Nearly free on calories; watch the sodium.

name: Oyster Sauce
notes: Low calorie, high sodium.

name: Chilli Sauce
notes: Sugar-based. Lea & Perrins style is similar.

name: Tomato Ketchup
notes: A quarter of it is sugar by weight.

name: Kuah Kacang (peanut sauce)
notes: Satay's real calories are in the sauce, not the meat.

name: Kaya
notes: Coconut and egg jam.

name: Peanut Butter
notes: Good satiety per calorie if you stop at one spoon.

name: Honey
notes: Sugar with trace minerals. Counts like sugar.

name: Sugar, white
notes: Three teaspoons is the standard teh tarik.

name: Susu Pekat Manis
notes: What makes kopi and teh tarik what they are.

name: Susu Cair (evaporated)
notes: Unsweetened. A lighter swap for condensed.

name: Belacan (shrimp paste)
notes: Tiny amounts, big flavour.

name: Curry Paste
notes: Before any santan goes in.

name: Fish Sauce / Budu
notes: Essentially free on calories.

name: Vinegar
notes: Free. Useful for making salads taste of something.

name: Mustard
notes: One of the few genuinely free condiments.

name: Thousand Island Dressing
notes: Turns a salad into a dessert calorie-wise.

name: Cheese Sauce
notes: Cheezy wedges territory.

name: Kuah Dalca
notes: Lentil-based, so it carries real protein and fibre.

name: Kubis (cabbage), boiled
notes: Bulk for almost no calories.

name: Cauliflower, steamed
notes: Rices well as a lower-carb swap.

name: Kacang Panjang, stir-fried
notes: Calories here are mostly the oil.

name: Bendi (okra), steamed
notes: High fibre, very low energy.

name: Terung (aubergine), grilled
notes: Soaks up oil like a sponge — grill rather than fry.

name: Labu (pumpkin), steamed
notes: Sweet but light.

name: Sawi, stir-fried
notes: Same story as kangkung: the oil is the cost.

name: Bayam, stir-fried
notes: Good iron and folate.

name: Taugeh (bean sprouts), blanched
notes: Free volume in any noodle dish.

name: Petai (stink beans)
notes: More protein than most vegetables.

name: Cendawan (mushrooms), sautéed
notes: Meaty texture for very little.

name: Sweet Corn, boiled
notes: Starchier than most vegetables — counts closer to a carb.

name: Green Peas, boiled
notes: Genuinely useful protein for a vegetable.

name: Capsicum, raw
notes: Vitamin C by the bucket.

name: Onion, raw
notes: Caramelising concentrates the sugars.

name: Garlic
notes: Negligible calories, non-negligible flavour.

name: Chilli, fresh
notes: Capsaicin's metabolic effect is real but tiny.

name: Potato, boiled
notes: Boiled and cooled, it gains resistant starch.

name: Tomato, raw
notes: Cooking makes the lycopene more available.

name: Lettuce
notes: Mostly water. Dressing is where the calories hide.

name: Celery
notes: Not negative-calorie, but close enough.

name: Asparagus, steamed
notes: High folate.

name: French Beans, steamed
notes: Reliable, cheap fibre.

name: Peria (bitter gourd), stir-fried
notes: Often studied for blood sugar; evidence is mixed.

name: Winter Melon, soup
notes: Almost entirely water.

name: Lobak (daikon), stewed
notes: Common in bak kut teh and soups.

name: Seaweed (nori)
notes: Iodine-dense. Snack packs add oil and salt.

name: Beetroot, boiled
notes: Nitrates; studied for endurance.

name: Pucuk Paku, stir-fried
notes: Wild fern shoots, common in kampung cooking.

name: Kailan, stir-fried
notes: Chinese kale.

name: Beef, lean, raw
notes: Daging batang pinang or similar lean cut.

name: Minced Beef, cooked
notes: Fat content varies hugely by grind — ask for lean.

name: Beef Rendang
notes: Santan and long cooking. A festival portion is often double.

name: Sirloin Steak, grilled
notes: Trim the rim of fat and it drops sharply.

name: Mutton, raw
notes: Fattier than beef at the same weight.

name: Gulai Kambing
notes: Rich. One serving can be a third of a day.

name: Lamb Chop, grilled
notes: Trimming the fat cap saves roughly 80 kcal.

name: Roast Duck
notes: Skin carries most of the fat; without it, ~200.

name: Fried Chicken Wings
notes: Batter plus skin plus oil.

name: Roast Chicken, with skin
notes: Skin off takes it to roughly 200.

name: Chicken Liver, cooked
notes: Extremely high vitamin A — do not eat daily in pregnancy.

name: Beef Liver, cooked
notes: One of the most nutrient-dense foods there is.

name: Chicken Sausage
notes: Processed; treat as an occasional food.

name: Beef Sausage
notes: Same caveat, more fat.

name: Bacon, grilled
notes: Salty and fatty; a little goes far.

name: Sliced Ham
notes: Leaner than most processed meat.

name: Beef Meatballs
notes: Common in soup noodles.

name: Chicken Nuggets
notes: Batter is roughly half the calories.

name: Udang (prawns), boiled
notes: High protein, very low fat.

name: Udang Goreng Tepung
notes: Batter more than doubles it.

name: Sotong, grilled
notes: Grilled rather than battered keeps it lean.

name: Ketam (crab), steamed
notes: Chilli crab sauce can add 300 kcal on its own.

name: Kerang (cockles), boiled
notes: Very high iron. Cook thoroughly.

name: Kupang (mussels), steamed
notes: Cheap protein and B12.

name: Ikan Bilis, fried
notes: Calcium-dense but usually deep-fried and salted.

name: Ikan Bilis, dried, raw
notes: Before frying — the oil is what changes it.

name: Tuna, canned in water
notes: Among the leanest protein per ringgit.

name: Tuna, canned in oil, drained
notes: Draining removes some but not all.

name: Ikan Tenggiri, grilled
notes: Good omega-3, widely available.

name: Ikan Bawal, steamed
notes: Steamed with ginger keeps it light.

name: Ikan Keli, grilled
notes: Ikan bakar staple.

name: Tilapia, steamed
notes: Lean and cheap; low in omega-3 though.

name: Fish Balls
notes: More starch than most people expect.

name: Fish Cake, fried
notes: Common in yong tau foo.

name: Ikan Masin, fried
notes: Very high sodium; used as a garnish for a reason.

name: Sotong Kering
notes: Chewy, high protein, very salty.

name: Telur Mata Kerbau (fried egg)
notes: About 40 kcal more than boiled, all from the oil.

name: Scrambled Egg
notes: Butter or milk added pushes it higher.

name: Telur Dadar
notes: With onion and chilli.

name: Telur Masin (salted egg)
notes: Very high sodium in the yolk.

name: Quail Eggs
notes: Common in yong tau foo and soups.

name: Full Cream Milk
notes: Roughly 40 kcal more than skim per glass.

name: Low Fat Milk
notes: Same protein and calcium as full cream.

name: Plain Yogurt
notes: Unsweetened. Flavoured versions can double the sugar.

name: Flavoured Yogurt
notes: Often as much sugar as a soft drink.

name: Cheddar Cheese
notes: Calorie-dense; a slice on toast is not free.

name: Mozzarella
notes: Lower fat than cheddar at the same weight.

name: Cream Cheese
notes: Mostly fat, little protein.

name: Soy Milk, unsweetened
notes: The closest plant milk to dairy on protein.

name: Soy Milk, sweetened
notes: Most kopitiam soy is sweetened.

name: Almond Milk, unsweetened
notes: Low calorie but very low protein.

name: Oat Milk
notes: Higher carb than dairy; good texture in coffee.

name: Dhal (lentil curry)
notes: Excellent protein and fibre for the cost.

name: Chickpeas, boiled
notes: Very filling; good in kerabu.

name: Kidney Beans, boiled
notes: Must be fully cooked — raw ones are toxic.

name: Baked Beans
notes: Tomato sauce brings sugar with it.

name: Kacang Hijau (mung beans), boiled
notes: Bubur kacang before the sugar and santan.

name: Soybeans, boiled
notes: The highest-protein legume by a distance.

name: Silken Tofu
notes: Softer, slightly lower protein than firm.

name: Tauhu Goreng
notes: Frying roughly triples plain tofu.

name: Tempeh, raw
notes: Fermented, so easier on digestion than plain soy.

name: Kacang Tanah, roasted
notes: Easy to eat three portions without noticing.

name: Fu Chuk (beancurd skin)
notes: Very protein-dense; often in soups.

name: Cashews, roasted
notes: Higher carb than most nuts.

name: Pistachios
notes: Shelling them slows you down, which helps.

name: Macadamia Nuts
notes: The fattiest common nut.

name: Sunflower Seeds
notes: Kuaci. Vitamin E.

name: Flaxseed, ground
notes: Plant omega-3. Must be ground to absorb.

name: Sesame Seeds
notes: Calcium-rich.

name: Mixed Nuts, roasted
notes: Portion by the handful, not the packet.

name: Mee Kuning, boiled
notes: Yellow noodles. Before any oil or sauce.

name: Bihun (rice vermicelli), cooked
notes: Light on protein; pair with something.

name: Kuey Teow, plain, cooked
notes: Char kuey teow adds ~250 kcal of oil and lard.

name: Mee Hoon Goreng
notes: The oil is what separates this from plain bihun.

name: Instant Noodles (Maggi)
notes: The fried block is most of the fat.

name: Instant Noodles, no seasoning oil
notes: Skipping the oil sachet saves ~60 kcal.

name: Pasta, cooked
notes: Al dente has a lower glycaemic impact.

name: Tanghoon (glass noodles), cooked
notes: Almost pure starch.

name: Barley, cooked
notes: High beta-glucan fibre.

name: Bulgur, cooked
notes: More fibre than rice, less faff than quinoa.

name: Nasi Minyak
notes: Ghee and stock. Briyani's base.

name: Pulut (glutinous rice), cooked
notes: Higher glycaemic load than white rice.

name: Nasi Dagang
notes: Cooked with santan.

name: Corn Flakes
notes: Often eaten in far bigger bowls than the label assumes.

name: Muesli
notes: Check for added sugar.

name: Wheat Biscuits (Weetabix)
notes: One of the plainer cereals.

name: White Bread
notes: Wholemeal is the same calories with three times the fibre.

name: Roti Bakar, butter & kaya
notes: The spreads carry more than the bread does.

name: Croissant, plain
notes: Laminated with butter, so it eats like a pastry.

name: Karipap, baked
notes: Baked rather than fried saves roughly 100 kcal.

name: Cream Crackers
notes: Plainer than most biscuits.

name: Potato Chips
notes: Hard to stop at one pack, by design.

name: Keropok Udang
notes: Puffed in oil.

name: Coated Peanuts
notes: The coating adds sugar and starch.

name: Dark Chocolate, 85%
notes: Less sugar, more fat than 70%.

name: Onde-onde
notes: Gula melaka centre.

name: Popcorn, air-popped
notes: Genuinely low calorie until butter appears.

name: Granola Bar
notes: Often a biscuit wearing a health label.

name: Protein Bar
notes: Useful when it displaces a worse snack.

name: Ayam Masak Merah
notes: Tomato and chilli base, moderate oil.

name: Ayam Goreng Berempah
notes: Spice crust holds oil.

name: Ayam Masak Lemak Cili Api
notes: Turmeric and santan.

name: Asam Pedas Ikan
notes: Tamarind base, no santan — one of the lighter curries.

name: Gulai Ikan
notes: Santan-based, so heavier than asam pedas.

name: Ikan Bakar
notes: Grilled with sambal. Among the best local orders.

name: Ayam Masak Kicap
notes: Kicap manis brings the sugar.

name: Lontong
notes: Rice cake in santan gravy.

name: Mee Rebus
notes: Sweet potato gravy.

name: Popiah
notes: One of the lighter street options.

name: Nasi Campur (3 dishes)
notes: Varies enormously — this is a middling pick.

name: Soto Ayam
notes: Lighter than most noodle bowls.

name: Laksa Penang
notes: Asam-based, so far lighter than curry laksa.

name: Hokkien Mee
notes: Dark soy and pork lard.

name: Bubur Ayam
notes: Gentle on the stomach, light on calories.

name: Bubur Kacang Hijau
notes: Gula melaka and santan.

name: Capati
notes: Lighter than roti canai by a wide margin.

name: Milo O Kosong
notes: Without condensed milk.

name: Milo Dinosaur
notes: Milo powder on top of a Milo drink.

name: Teh C Peng
notes: Evaporated milk plus sugar.

name: Orange Juice, packet
notes: Little different from a soft drink on sugar.

name: Soft Drink (cola)
notes: Nine teaspoons of sugar.

name: Soft Drink, zero sugar
notes: Effectively free on calories.

name: Bottled Lemon Tea
notes: Bottle size makes this worse than a can of cola.
